item.description:
US responds to suspected drone activity over UK air base used in Iran strikes

US Air Force personnel at the RAF Lakenheath base in Britain responded to “suspected unauthorised drone activity” on Friday evening, a US Air Force spokesperson said, adding that no personnel, aircraft or infrastructure were affected.

“We continue to work closely with our host nation counterparts to ensure the safety and security of our US service members, US and host nation civilians, contractors, and all of our families,” the spokesperson said by email.

Britain's Ministry of Defence said US Air Force Security Forces personnel had responded to reports of unauthorised drone activity and that the situation had been resolved.

In recent weeks, the US has moved bombers that had been used to strike Iran out of Britain, and relocated large refuelling aircraft from Britain to Germany. The Wall Street Journal reported that the moves were due to a threat from Iran.

The bombers left RAF Fairford on security grounds after a group of men approached the base in white vans on the night of  27 September.

Two men were charged last month in relation to that incident, with prosecutors alleging that one of them had tried to assist Iranian intelligence in Britain.

The US Justice Department said this week that a member of an Iran-backed militia had plotted to attack the Fairford base while detained in the US on criminal charges.

Tehran has denied involvement in the Fairford incident and rejected other accusations of malign activity in Britain.

item.title: [www.middleeasteye.net] US flights halted nationwide after FAA communications outage
item.description:
US flights halted nationwide after FAA communications outage

The US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has ordered a nationwide ground stop following a telecommunications outage affecting air traffic control operations, suspending departures across the country. Flights already airborne have been allowed to continue to their destinations while authorities work to resolve the disruption.

More than 10,000 flights were delayed and over 2,000 cancelled, according to flight-tracking website FlightAware, with CBS News reporting that a  software update to a private communications network connecting air traffic control facilities across the US caused the system to reboot and crash, triggering the outage.

The nationwide ground stop is the first since January 2023, when an FAA computer system malfunction disrupted operations. The previous major halt followed the September 11, 2001 attacks.

Flight-tracking service Flightradar24 reported just 1,000 flights heading to US airports, down nearly 80 percent from more than 4,500 a week earlier.

* JetBlue Airways reported departure delays, saying it was monitoring developments and would resume operations once authorities permitted flights to take off.

* Air Canada warned that flights to and from the Caribbean and South America could be affected, advising passengers to check its app for updates.

* Britain's Civil Aviation Authority warned travellers of disruption to flights to, from and within the US, urging passengers to check with airlines.

item.description:
UN, partners urge Israel to lift restrictions on aid into Gaza

The UN and its humanitarian partners have called on Israel to lift restrictions on aid deliveries to Gaza, warning that deadly rainstorms have killed children and adults, destroyed shelters and flooded thousands of family tents.

More than 150,000 tents remain outside Gaza, ready for dispatch, as restrictions on supplies and access continue to hamper winter preparations, according to the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA).

In a statement, the Humanitarian Country Team, comprising UN agencies and humanitarian organisations operating in the Occupied Palestinian Territory, said the devastation caused by the rainstorms was preventable.

Humanitarian partners had presented a winter preparedness plan months ago, but restrictions on supplies and access, alongside funding shortfalls, had hampered its implementation.

The Team urged Israel to lift restrictions, enable repairs to water and wastewater networks, and allow all humanitarian partners to operate.

The appeal follows a statement earlier this week by Emergency Relief Coordinator Tom Fletcher, who warned that delays, restrictions and funding cuts were putting lives at risk.

The Humanitarian Country Team also urged member states to use their influence to remove obstacles to aid deliveries and provide urgently needed funding.

item.title: [www.middleeasteye.net] Iran warns of 'immediate response' to any US-Israeli attack, slams Gulf nations
item.description:
Iran warns of 'immediate response' to any US-Israeli attack, slams Gulf nations

Iran has said that any renewed US-Israeli attacks on its territory would trigger an immediate response, while accusing Bahrain and other Gulf countries of facilitating Washington’s military operations against Tehran.

“Any renewed war of aggression by the United States and the Israeli regime will be met with an immediate and decisive response, without hesitation,” said Gholamhossein Darzi, Iran's deputy permanent representative to the UN, during a Security Council meeting on the situation in the Middle East.

 "We regret the positions taken by some Council members, particularly its Western members. Their statements reflect a familiar pattern of double standards and blatant hypocrisy," he told the council.

He also accused some Gulf countries of allowing their territory, airspace and military facilities to be used for US-Israeli attacks, arguing that they should be held accountable and compensate Iran for the resulting damage.

In a subsequent exchange with Bahrain’s representative, Darzi singled out the kingdom, saying it had facilitated US military operations against Tehran.

Bahrain rejected Iran’s accusations and said Tehran could not invoke its right to self-defence to justify attacks on neighbouring countries.

item.title: [www.middleeasteye.net] Rubio targets ICC: 'Won't submit to sterile vision of radical judges':
item.description:
Rubio targets ICC: 'Won't submit to sterile vision of radical judges':

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has targeted the International Criminal Court (ICC) in a speech to a conservative legal group on Friday, arguing for a muscular foreign policy and against international law restraining US actions.

During his speech to the Federalist Society in Washington, his first prepared remarks since Republicans were routed in the midterm elections on 3 November, Rubio said the goal of the US-Israeli war against Iran was to prevent Tehran from ever developing a nuclear weapon, which he said was particularly urgent because the Islamic Republic's "radical Shia clerics" had an "expansionist mentality."

He contrasted this with the government of North Korea's Kim Jong Un, whom Trump has met three times. "I'm not excusing the terrible things that have happened there," Rubio said of North Korea. "I'm just saying he (Kim) is not expansionist. He's not trying to invade Japan or, you know, China or whatever."

Rubio dismissed criticisms that the Trump administration has broken international law by such actions as seizing Venezuelan then-President Nicolas Maduro and striking boats in the Caribbean and Eastern Pacific that it says were carrying drugs.

The US, Rubio said, would not “submit to the sterile vision of radical judges or soulless global bureaucrats,” repeating his assertion that the court would try to prosecute US officials or service members that he used to justify sanctions against the ICC announced last month.

“Americans have never agreed to submit to the ICC's authority, but that court and its allies in the global bureaucracy have appointed themselves judge and jury and executioner of the international order,” Rubio said.

The Trump ​administration has long been hostile to the Netherlands-based court, founded in 2002 to prosecute war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide, and has previously imposed sanctions on its prosecutors and judges.

The ICC has received strong backing from most member states, which include all EU countries and all members of the NATO alliance apart from the United States and Turkey.

Washington has denounced the court over arrest warrants issued for Israeli officials including Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, and ​an investigation into actions of US soldiers in Afghanistan, which the ICC says is "deprioritised."

The US sanctions, designed to stifle the ICC’s ability to operate, will take effect in April unless supporters of the Netherlands-based court can reach an agreement with the US to avert them.

Rubio suggested that if the court tried to enforce its rulings against Americans, Washington would respond with force. Quoting the Roman general Pompey, Rubio said the US response would be: "Stop quoting laws to men with swords.”

Report by Reuters

item.title: [World news | The Guardian] Airport chaos continues after US ground stop lifted – as it happened
item.description:
This blog is now closed. See our full reports:

  • US aviation agency lifts nationwide ground stop affecting all air travel

  • Chaos at US airports as flight stoppage grinds travel plans to a halt

  • Sign up for the Breaking News US email

We’re wrapping up this live coverage of the US ground stop and travel chaos that followed – it’s just passed 12.50am in Washington DC. Below’s a rundown on what happened, and you can read a full report here. Thanks for being with us.

The Federal Aviation Administration declared a nationwide ground stop on Friday afternoon, throwing airports into sudden chaos, after a communications failure at air traffic control centres.

More than 6,600 flights were cancelled and 8,600 delayed, with another 1,500 already cancelled for Sunday, according to FlightRadar24. Aviation analysts said the four-hour nationwide grounding could disrupt airline ⁠schedules for days. It was the longest flight shutdown since the attacks of September 11 2001.

The FAA lifted the ground stop later on Friday, with transportation secretary Sean Duffy saying US airspace reopened at 8.15pm ET (0115 GMT). But departures would ⁠resume gradually and it would take ​time for airlines to restore normal operations, he warned. “It’s going to be slow.”

All US-bound departures from European airports are suspended until 5am UTC on Saturday, according to a notice published by the European traffic control agency, Eurocontrol.

US airlines including American, United and Southwest began resuming flights on Friday night. “Thank you for your understanding as we work as quickly as possible to fully restore normal operations,” Delta said.

Duffy said the federal government had “identified the problem” that brought down the US air traffic control system on Friday and it was “operational right now”. The system was “incredibly old”, he said. “Our routers actually got overloaded with data, and … they started to give us inconsistency in the data from those routers. And because of that, we shut the system down.”

There was no indication from preliminary investigations that the communications stoppage was tied to a “nefarious attack”, homeland security secretary Markwayne Mullin said.

Duffy blamed Congress for failing to fund a new air traffic control system that he said could prevent such outages, and called for $50bn to modernize it.

'What would be left of international legal order': Araghchi on US strikes

"If states were free to attack one another based on their own assessments of possible future threats, what would be left of the international legal order?" Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi has asked in an opinion piece for Japan's Kyodo News.

"This question," Araghchi wrote, "goes well beyond the political dispute between Iran and the United States."

"It concerns one of the fundamental principles on which the international order established after the Second World War rests: the use of force is governed by law, and no state, however powerful, is entitled to place its own judgment above binding rules of international law," the article read.

He said the US-Israeli strikes constituted a clear violation of the prohibition on the use of force and an infringement of Iran's sovereignty.

"Their legality must be assessed against the U.N. Charter and established principles of international law, not against political arguments or justifications advanced after military operations have begun," he wrote.

He said the US had neither obtained UN Security Council authorisation nor established grounds for invoking self-defence under Article 51, which permits force in response to an armed attack.

The attacks on schools, sports stadiums, civilian infrastructure, and Iranian nuclear facilities subject to International Atomic Energy Agency safeguards raise further questions under international law, and they must be examined under international humanitarian law.

Saudi-led coalition air strikes targeted southern parts of Saada city in northern Yemen, while artillery shelling hit populated villages in the border district of Razih, Al Jazeera reported, citing Houthi-run Al Masirah TV.

Yemen’s government military spokesperson, Colonel Majed Al-Nuzaili, said on Friday that government forces carried out 943 strikes and targeting operations against Houthi positions as part of Operation Dawn of Yemen.

item.title: [World news | The Guardian] Tout offers £1m of U2 tickets on StubHub, raising questions about ‘bot’ clampdown
item.description:
Artists and industry figures call for culture secretary to ‘shut down the touts’ by outlawing resale for profit

One tout is advertising £1m of tickets for U2’s long-awaited 2027 tour through StubHub, raising questions about the website’s condemnation of professional ticket traders who use “bot” software to scoop up tickets and exploit genuine fans.

Seats for the four-night London leg of the Irish band’s The Greatest Show on Earth tour sold out last week, shortly after going on sale.

item.title: [World news | The Guardian] Hundreds of children in England prescribed weight-loss jabs, figures show
item.description:
Exclusive: investigation finds prescriptions for children under 12, as experts stress need for specialist supervision and long-term monitoring

Hundreds of children in England are receiving prescriptions for GLP-1 medications, including some younger than 12, the Guardian can reveal.

GLP-1 medications were initially developed to help people with type 2 diabetes control their blood sugar levels, but have since become a popular slimming aid, with products such as Wegovy and Mounjaro becoming household names.

item.title: [World news | The Guardian] Immersive show brings Kyffin Williams’ rugged Welsh landscapes to life
item.description:
Paintings by one of country’s most important artists have been animated and set to music at National Library of Wales

The paintings of artists such as Vincent van Gogh, Paul Cézanne and David Hockney have been brought to life in all-singing, all-dancing immersive shows in recent years.

Now one of Wales’s most important artists, Sir Kyffin Williams, known for capturing the spectacular landscapes of his homeland with layers of paint thickly applied with a palette knife, has been given the same treatment.
